evidence.timingScope: One modeled party or raid entry after a solo refresh per operation-count pair, plus five alternating timing pairs with six entries and intervening leaves. The actual Core nameplate event dispatcher, Threat API and Threat, Level and Countdown modules run on counted widget and unit stubs. Quest overlay is disabled and 32 hostile nameplates remain active. The untimed final leave clears group-only tints. These are subworkflow counts and desktop CPU timings, with native latency still open.
evidence.timingSummary: The simulated Forever tank case has six-cycle medians of 76 and 17 ms. Non-tank timing varied by desktop client model and case. Non-tank detailed payload counts remain equal.

parity: Nameplate threat refreshes now share successful public group identity reads for one pass. With 32 visible plates, a modeled party entry uses 10 GUID queries instead of 320. The raid case uses 82 instead of 2,624. A confirmed tanking player already has rank one, allowing the same raid replay to use 64 detailed threat queries instead of 2,592. Matched text, tint and plate lookups remain equal in all three client models.
rules: Share public identity for one full refresh. Keep per-target threat payloads for non-tanking ranks and fresh guarded reads for unreadable IDs and unit existence. Standalone rank calls retain their own reads. A replaced GUID or rank provider uses the current provider. A known tanking player row returns rank one before the group walk. No settings, events or timers are added.
nativeAcceptance: Live party and raid join or leave timing and native secret-value and combat checks remain pending. Action strip, border seams, embedded minimap and combat exit acceptance remain open for the wider goal.
